input.strategy_title: Feature Store as a supported RHOAI component
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers building recommendation and fraud models ask for a supported feature
store; today they self-manage upstream Feast next to the platform with no
lifecycle integration, no supported images, and no UI presence. Feast has a
Jira component reserved (Feature Store) but is not yet part of the platform:
there is no productized repository, no build pipeline, and no operator
integration. This strategy brings Feast in as a supported, installable RHOAI
component.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported Feature Store (Feast) through the Platform Operator like any other managed component, with productized images. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Data scientists can reach the feature store from workbenches with the Feast SDK preinstalled in at least one supported workbench image. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard shows the Feature Store as an enabled component and links users to its endpoints per project. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Product documentation covers enablement, a getting-started walkthrough, and supported limits. |

## Affected Components

- Feature Store
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- A feature-authoring UI in the Dashboard (link-out only this release)
- Managed offline-store infrastructure — customers bring their own storage

## Open Questions

1. Which Feast deployment topology do we productize first — the operator-based
   deployment or the standalone server per project? Upstream supports both;
   supportability differs.

# Productize operator-based Feast deployment

## Description

Conditional epic — executes only if the deployment-topology investigation
selects the operator-based topology. Productize the Feast operator as the
supported deployment mechanism for the Feature Store: the operator deploys and
reconciles Feast resources on OpenShift, built from the productized midstream
repository and shipped as Konflux-built container images.

## Scope

- Productize the Feast operator and its managed resources for OpenShift:
    packaging, manifests, and reconciliation behavior against the midstream
    Feast codebase.
- Consume the productized images built by the Konflux pipeline (pinned
    digests are a configuration reference wired at execution time — the
    deployment code is not blocked on the pipeline beyond the green-build
    gate below).
- Define the CRD/API surface the operator exposes, which the Platform
    Operator enablement and the Dashboard integration build against.
- Document failure modes, upgrade path, and per-project behavior for
    supportability.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The productized Feast operator deploys on OpenShift and reconciles Feast
    resources to a running state.
- The build pipeline is green for all images shipped by this deployment (the
    Konflux pipeline builds the merged implementation code successfully).
- Productized image digests are published and pinnable by consumers.
- Failure modes and upgrade behavior are documented sufficiently for the
    supportability standard used by the topology decision.
- Given the operator-based deployment is productized, when enablement and
    Dashboard work consume its CRD surface, then that surface is stable and
    documented.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): provides the deployable, supported Feature Store with
  productized images that administrators enable through the Platform Operator.

# Enable Feature Store via Platform Operator (operator topology)

## Description

Conditional epic — executes only if the operator-based topology is selected.
Add the Feature Store to the set of managed components administrators can
enable through the Platform Operator (HLR-1): enabling Feature Store installs
and drives the productized Feast operator, like any other managed component.

## Scope

- Extend the Platform Operator's managed-component enablement mechanism to
  cover the Feature Store under the operator-based topology (installation and
  lifecycle of the Feast operator and its prerequisites).
- Build against the CRD/API surface the operator-based deployment exposes.
- Wire enablement to the productized image digests published by the build
  pipeline (pinned digests filled in as a configuration reference — an
  acceptance gate, not a build dependency).
- Provide disable/cleanup behavior consistent with other managed components.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a cluster with the Platform Operator installed, when an administrator
  enables the Feature Store, then the Feast operator is installed and the
  Feature Store becomes usable — measured by the same enablement flow used for
  other managed components.
- Disabling the Feature Store reconciles its resources away cleanly (rollback
  path for the enablement toggle).
- Enablement references pinned productized image digests that are available.
- The enablement behavior is verified on OpenShift against the productized
  operator-based deployment.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): administrators can enable a supported Feature Store through the
  Platform Operator like any other managed component.

# Dashboard Feature Store presence and endpoint links (operator topology)

## Description

Conditional epic — executes only if the operator-based topology is selected.
Surface the Feature Store in the Dashboard (HLR-3): show it as an enabled
component and link users to its endpoints per project. Link-out only — the
feature-authoring UI is explicitly out of scope this release.

## Scope

- Add Feature Store presence to the Dashboard's enabled-components view,
  driven by the component's enablement state.
- Link users to the Feature Store endpoints for each project, reading the
  CRs/resources the operator-based deployment exposes.
- Follow the Dashboard's existing component-integration pattern (per-component
  feature flags and defaults via the dashboard configuration CR, reading
  component CRs via the Kubernetes API).
- No feature-authoring UI: navigation and link-out only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the Feature Store is enabled for a project, when a user opens the
  Dashboard, then the Feature Store appears as an enabled component for that
  project — measured by the enabled-components view.
- Endpoint links resolve to the Feature Store endpoints exposed for the
  project under the operator-based deployment.
- The integration is feature-flagged/configurable via the Dashboard
  configuration CR consistent with other component integrations.
- No feature-authoring UI is introduced (link-out only, per out-of-scope).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): the Dashboard shows the Feature Store as an enabled component
  and links users to its endpoints per project.

# Decide Feast deployment topology for productization

## Description

Resolve the strategy's open question: which Feast deployment topology to
productize first — the operator-based deployment or the standalone server per
project. Upstream Feast supports both; their supportability profiles differ
(upgrade path, per-project isolation, resource footprint, failure modes, and
fit with the Platform Operator's managed-component enablement model). This
investigation produces the decision and the supportability assessment behind
it, and selects which conditional implementation branch executes.

## Scope

- Assess both candidate topologies against defined supportability criteria:
  upgrade/version management, per-project isolation and multi-tenancy,
  resource footprint, failure modes and operational burden, alignment with how
  the Platform Operator enables other managed components, and Dashboard
  integration surface (what CRs/endpoints each topology exposes per project).
- Use upstream Feast documentation, repository source, and deployment
  references as evidence; validate operator-rendered resources from source
  where possible.
- Record the decision with rationale and obtain stakeholder/product sign-off
  on the selected topology.
- Confirm the downstream impact: which deployment, Platform Operator
  enablement, and Dashboard integration work proceeds under the selected
  outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Both topologies are assessed against the enumerated supportability criteria,
  with evidence drawn from upstream source and documentation.
- A decision is recorded (operator-based OR standalone server per project) with
  rationale, and reviewed by stakeholders.
- The conditional implementation branch matching the decision is confirmed as
  the plan of record; the non-selected branch is discarded.
- Given the decision is made, when downstream teams start deployment,
  enablement, and Dashboard work, then they have an unambiguous topology and
  its per-project endpoint/CR surface — measured by the decision record being
  referenced in those work items.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): gates the admin-enablement implementation path; the topology
  decision determines how the Feature Store is deployed and enabled through
  the Platform Operator.
- HLR-3 (P1): determines the endpoint/CR surface the Dashboard will surface.

# License validation for Feast and transitive dependencies

## Description

Run license scanning over Feast and its full transitive dependency tree to
clear the Feature Store for productization as a supported RHOAI component.
This runs in parallel with repository onboarding (independent inputs) and
gates all downstream Feature Store implementation: if licenses fail, the
dependency set or the productization approach changes.

## Scope

- Configure and run the standard license-scanning tooling against the Feast
  source (upstream, and the midstream repository once available).
- Produce a full transitive dependency license report.
- Triage flagged licenses against Red Hat productization policy; record
  clearance status or remediation options for each flag.
- Escalate any unresolved conflicts (e.g. copyleft licenses that cannot ship)
  with remediation recommendations — replacement dependency, exclusion, or
  upstream contribution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A complete license scan of Feast and its transitive dependency tree exists,
  with a triage report covering every flagged license.
- No unresolved license conflict remains that blocks shipping the Feast SDK in
  workbench images or the Feature Store server/operator images — any
  conflicts are either cleared or have a documented remediation plan accepted
  by stakeholders.
- Given the scan is clear, when the workbench SDK image and the deployment
  implementation proceed, then their dependency sets are license-cleared for
  productization.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): productized Feature Store images require license-cleared
  dependencies.
- HLR-2 (P1): the Feast SDK cannot ship in a supported workbench image unless
  its dependency tree is license-cleared.
